style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: A short psalm about speech as ordnance. The enemies sharpen their tongues like swords and tread their bows to fire bitter words from hiding at the blameless man -- suddenly, fearlessly, at planning meetings where they hide snares and ask, 'Who will see them?' David asks to be guarded not only from the enemy but from dread of him, and to be hidden from both the whispered council and the noisy mob. Then God takes every one of their words and turns it around: He shoots -- one arrow -- suddenly, and they are wounded; the tongue they sharpened is the thing they trip over. The psalm ends with the crowd the plotters never counted on: all mankind fears and declares the work of God, and the righteous, glad in the LORD, do the only boasting the Bible allows.

1.text: For the choir director. A psalm of David. Hear my voice, O God, in my complaint; guard my life from dread of the enemy.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], A Psalm [mizmor] of David. Hear [shama] my voice [qol], O God [Elohim], in my prayer [siach -- complaint, musing]: preserve [natsar -- guard] my life [chay] from fear [pachad -- dread] of the enemy [oyeb].
1.notes: shema-Elohim qoli be-sichi (H8085, H430, H6963, H7879): hear my voice in my siach -- the word for a complaint poured out, Psalm 102's title-word; mi-pachad oyeb titsor chayyai (H6343, H341, H5341, H2416): from the DREAD of the enemy guard my life. Not only from the enemy -- from the fear of him, which does its own damage first.

2.text: Hide me from the secret council of evildoers, from the noisy mob of the workers of iniquity,
2.amp: Hide [satar] me from the secret counsel [sod -- conclave] of the wicked [raa -- evildoers]; from the insurrection of the workers [paal] of iniquity [aven]:
2.notes: tastireni mi-sod mereim (H5641, H5475, H7489): hide me from the sod of evildoers -- the private council, the same word for God's intimate circle in Psalm 25:14, here a cabal; me-rigshat poale aven (H6466, H205): from the tumult of the workers of wickedness -- rigshah, the crowd-noise of Psalm 2:1's raging. Two dangers: the whispered plan and the loud crowd.

3.text: who sharpen their tongue like a sword, who have aimed their arrow -- a bitter word --
3.amp: Who whet [shanan -- sharpen] their tongue [lashon] like a sword [cherev], and bend [darak -- tread] their bows to shoot their arrows [chets], even bitter [mar] words [dabar]:
3.notes: asher shanenu kha-chereb leshonam (H8150, H2719, H3956): who have SHARPENED their tongue like a sword -- shanan, the verb for whetting and for drilling children in the Shema (Deuteronomy 6:7); darekhu chitsam dabar mar (H1869, H2671, H1697, H4751): they have trod their arrow -- a bitter word. The weapons of Psalm 57:4 and 55:21: the whole psalm is about speech as ordnance.

4.text: to shoot from hiding places at the blameless; suddenly they shoot at him, and they are not afraid.
4.amp: That they may shoot [yarah] in secret at the perfect [tam -- blameless]: suddenly [pithom] do they shoot [yarah] at him, and fear [yare] not.
4.notes: lirot ba-mistarim tam (H3384, H8535): to shoot from the hiding places at the tam, the whole-hearted man -- Psalm 11:2's archers in the dark; pitom yoruhu ve-lo yirau (H6597, H3384, H3372): SUDDENLY they shoot him and do not fear. Verse 7 will give the word 'suddenly' back to them.

5.text: They brace themselves for an evil plan; they talk about hiding snares; they say, 'Who will see them?'
5.amp: They encourage [chazaq -- strengthen] themselves in an evil [ra] matter ['speech', dabar, the KJV margin]: they commune [saphar -- recount] of laying snares [moqesh] privily ['to hide his snares', taman, the KJV margin]; they say [amar], Who shall see [raah] them?
5.notes: yechazzequ-lamo dabar ra (H2388, H1697, H7451): they make themselves strong in an evil dabar -- a word, a plan, the margin's 'speech'. yesapperu litmon moqeshim (H5608, H2934, H4170): they recount how to hide snares -- 'to hide his snares', the margin's singular; ameru mi yireh-lamo (H559, H7200): 'who will see them?' -- the practical atheist's question of Psalm 10:11 and 94:7, asked at the planning meeting.

6.text: They search out injustices: 'We have finished a thorough search!' -- for the inside of a man and his heart are deep.
6.amp: They search out [chaphas] iniquities [avlah -- injustices]; they accomplish [tamam -- complete] a diligent search ['a search searched', chaphas, the KJV margin]: both the inward [qereb] thought of every one [ish] of them, and the heart [leb], is deep.
6.notes: yachpesu-olot tamnu chephes mechuppas (H2664, H5766, H8552): they hunt out injustices -- 'we have finished a search searched', the margin's literal, a thorough one. ve-qereb ish ve-leb amoq (H7130, H376, H3820, H6013): and the inward part of a man and his heart are DEEP -- the psalm's verdict on the plotters, or their boast; the other margin reads it as the victims: 'we are consumed by what they have thoroughly searched'. Jeremiah 17:9's heart, measured: deep.

7.text: But God will shoot them with an arrow; suddenly they are struck down.
7.amp: But God [Elohim] shall shoot [yarah] at them with an arrow [chets]; suddenly [pithom] shall they be wounded ['their wound shall be', makkah, the KJV margin].
7.notes: va-yorem Elohim chets (H430, H3384, H2671): and God SHOOTS them -- an arrow: one, against their quiverful; pitom hayu makkotam (H6597, H4347): suddenly 'their wounds have been', the margin's literal. Every word is theirs from verse 4 -- shoot, arrow, suddenly -- turned around. The archers in the dark discover Someone else can see in it.

8.text: They are made to stumble, their own tongue turned against them; all who see them shake their heads and flee.
8.amp: So they shall make their own tongue [lashon] to fall [kashal -- stumble] upon themselves: all that see [raah] them shall flee away [nadad].
8.notes: va-yakhshiluhu alemo leshonam (H3782, H3956): and they make him stumble -- 'upon themselves their tongue': the sharpened tongue of verse 3 is the thing they trip over; yitnodedu kol-roeh bam (H5074, H7200): everyone who sees them wags -- nadad, flees or shakes the head; the WEB takes the head-shake, the KJV the flight. Psalm 9:15's boomerang, in the mouth.

9.text: Then all mankind will fear and will declare the work of God, for they will understand what He has done.
9.amp: And all men [adam] shall fear [yare], and shall declare [nagad] the work [poal] of God [Elohim]; for they shall wisely consider [sakal] of His doing [maaseh].
9.notes: va-yireu kol-adam (H3372, H120): and all mankind FEARS -- the fear the archers did not have (v. 4) lands on everyone who watched; va-yaggidu poal Elohim u-maasehu hiskilu (H5046, H6467, H430, H4639, H7919): and they declare God's work and give wise thought to His deed -- sakal, Psalm 41:1's verb. The plotters' 'who will see?' is answered by a crowd of witnesses.

10.text: The righteous will rejoice in the LORD and take refuge in Him, and all the upright in heart will glory.
10.amp: The righteous [tsaddiq] shall be glad [samach] in the LORD [YHWH], and shall trust [chasah -- take refuge] in Him; and all the upright [yashar] in heart [leb] shall glory [halal -- boast].
10.notes: yismach tsaddiq ba-YHWH ve-chasah bo (H8055, H6662, H3068, H2620): the righteous is glad in the LORD -- the only time the Name appears in the psalm, saved for the end -- and takes refuge in Him; ve-yithalelu kol-yishre-leb (H1984, H3477, H3820): and all the straight of heart BOAST -- halal, the hallelujah verb, the boast that is allowed (cf. Psalm 34:2; Jeremiah 9:24). The psalm began hiding from a whisper and ends boasting out loud.
